newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SKODA PRAHA SEES 96 NET PROFIT RISE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SKODA PRAHA SEES 96 NET PROFIT RISE.

text.p: Czech engineering concern Skoda Praha a.s. on Monday said that, according to preliminary figures, the firm posted a 1996 net profit of 166.88 million crowns, up from 25.7 million crowns in 1995.
The firm's Financial Director Jiri Hrbek told a news conference that the plans to pay a 30-32 crown per share gross dividend for 1996.
Skoda Praha paid a 20 crown per share gross dividend in 1995.
Hrbek said the firm's revenues for 1996 were 8.34 billion crowns, down sharply from 20.2 billion, while its operating profit totalled 156.02 million crowns, up from 80.1 million crowns.
He said that as of December 31, the firm's assets totalled 17.4 billion crowns and that its basic capital at the end of the year was 557.5 million crowns.
The main shareholders of Skoda Praha include the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (54.7 percent), investment firm SIS (15.5 percent), and investment firm ATC (14.9 percent).
